content.value_statement: Refactoring can hide test failures, build breaks, and quality drops. This skill records baselines, reruns checks, compares results, and recommends rollback when quality drops.
actual_capabilities: Records baseline test, lint, build, and coverage metrics for backend and frontend.
Repeats the same checks after refactoring and compares results.
Classifies severe and minor regressions using documented thresholds.
Produces verification reports with rollback recommendations.
Points to required project reports and development policy files.
limitations: Assumes the project uses backend Gradle commands and frontend pnpm commands.
Does not implement tests or fix regressions itself.
Requires access to the target repository and local toolchain.
Performance checks are documented only when applicable.

use_cases.title: Validate Refactoring Safety
use_cases.description: Compare pre-refactor and post-refactor quality results before accepting a change.

use_cases.title: Create Regression Reports
use_cases.description: Summarize tests, lint, build status, and coverage in a review-ready format.

use_cases.title: Decide Rollback Timing
use_cases.description: Use strict criteria to decide whether a regression needs immediate rollback.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use guard-regression to record current backend and frontend quality results before refactoring starts.

prompt_templates.title: Compare After Refactoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Use guard-regression to rerun the documented checks and compare them with the saved baseline.

prompt_templates.title: Report a Detected Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Use guard-regression to identify which metrics degraded and prepare a rollback recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release gate with strict thresholds.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use guard-regression to evaluate test, lint, build, coverage, and performance results against rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: Compare the post-refactor checks with the saved baseline.
output: Tests, lint, build, and coverage stayed at or above baseline.
Next action: approve the refactor report.

output_examples.input: The backend build failed after refactoring.
output: The build result changed from success to failure.
Next action: recommend immediate rollback and rerun validation after rollback.

output_examples.input: Coverage dropped by three percent after cleanup.
output: Coverage dropped within the warning range.
Next action: request review before accepting the refactor.

best_practices: Capture the baseline before any refactoring begins.
Run the same checks in the same environment for fair comparison.
Record exact counts and percentages in every report.
anti_patterns: Do not compare results from different environments without noting the difference.
Do not ignore a new test failure because other metrics improved.
Do not approve a refactor when the build changed from success to failure.

faq.question: What does this skill monitor?
faq.answer: It monitors tests, lint results, build status, coverage, and optional performance indicators.

faq.question: Does it change application code?
faq.answer: No. It records and compares quality results, then reports rollback guidance.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects local backend Gradle checks and frontend pnpm checks in the target project.

faq.question: When does it recommend rollback?
faq.answer: It recommends rollback for new test failures, build failure, major coverage loss, or serious lint errors.

faq.question: Can it handle false positives?
faq.answer: Yes. It advises rerunning checks and considering environment differences before final judgment.

faq.question: Is it useful outside the original project?
faq.answer: Yes, if the project uses similar test, build, lint, and coverage workflows.
